tool_input.description: Probe JDK behaviors used to craft correct test expectations

result:
All 100 tests pass except the one intentionally exposing the bug.

## Summary

I added `src/test/java/org/apache/commons/lang3/math/NumberUtilsAgentTest.java` with 100 self-contained JUnit 5 tests covering `NumberUtils`'s constants, `compare`, `createBigDecimal/BigInteger/Double/Float/Integer/Long/Number`, `isCreatable/isNumber/isDigits/isParsable`, the `max`/`min` array and 3-arg overloads (including `NaN` and boundary/empty-array/null-array cases), the `to*` conversion methods, and `toScaledBigDecimal`.

**99 tests pass. 1 test fails, and it reveals a real bug:**

- `testToScaledBigDecimalFloatRoundsTheFloatsOwnDecimalValue` — `NumberUtils.toScaledBigDecimal(Float.valueOf(0.045f))` returns `0.05` instead of the correct `0.04`. The bug is in `toScaledBigDecimal(Float, int, RoundingMode)`, which converts via `BigDecimal.valueOf(value)` where `value` is a `Float`; this implicitly widens the `float` to a `double` first. That widening perturbs `0.045f`'s true decimal value (`"0.045"` per `Float.toString`) upward just enough that `HALF_EVEN` rounding at scale 2 tips to `0.05` instead of correctly rounding `0.045` to the even neighbor `0.04`. The fix would be to construct the `BigDecimal` from the float's own string/exact `float` representation (e.g. `new BigDecimal(value.toString())`) rather than widening to `double`.
